title: Atmospheric water harvesting efficiency
bottleneck: Pulling water from air could serve arid regions, but thermodynamics is unforgiving: at low humidity the energy cost per liter is enormous, sorbent-based systems cycle slowly, and passive radiative designs produce only liters per day per square meter. No technology yet delivers household-scale water in arid climates at an energy cost competitive with trucking water in. Fouling and sorbent degradation in dusty real-world air further cut yields.
why_it_blocks: Two billion people face water stress, and atmospheric harvesting is one of few options for off-grid arid communities. The efficiency gap keeps it a gadget-scale curiosity rather than a water-security tool.
current_state: Metal-organic-framework harvesters demonstrated grams-per-day yields in desert trials, and successive designs keep improving. But the leap to the hundreds of liters per day a household needs, at affordable energy, remains far off.
